lessons.title: Simple Interest
lessons.concept: Simple Interest (SI) is calculated only on the original principal for the entire time period. The interest amount stays the same each year when rate and principal are constant.
lessons.formula: SI = (P x R x T) / 100, where P = principal, R = rate % per annum, T = time in years. Amount A = P + SI.
lessons.worked_example: Find SI on Rs. 8,000 at 5% per annum for 3 years. SI = (8000 x 5 x 3)/100 = 1200. Amount = 8000 + 1200 = Rs. 9,200.
mistakes: Forgetting to divide by 100 when rate is given as a percentage.
Using time in months without converting to years (months/12).
Adding interest to principal before applying SI formula (SI uses original principal).

lessons.title: Compound Interest
lessons.concept: Compound Interest (CI) is calculated on principal plus accumulated interest. Each period, interest is added to the amount and future interest is computed on this increased amount (compounding).
lessons.formula: Amount A = P(1 + R/100)^T (compounded annually). CI = A - P = P[(1 + R/100)^T - 1].
mistakes: Using SI formula for compound interest problems.
Forgetting that CI for 1 year equals SI for 1 year (when compounded annually), but differs for more than 1 year.
Not adjusting rate/time when compounding is half-yearly or quarterly (rate becomes R/2 or R/4, time becomes 2T or 4T).

lessons.title: Difference and Comparison (SI vs CI)
lessons.concept: For the same principal, rate, and time (>1 year), CI is greater than SI because CI earns interest on interest. The difference comes from interest on the first year's interest in the second year, and so on.
lessons.formula: For 2 years (annual compounding): Difference = CI - SI = P(R/100)^2. For 3 years: Difference = P(R/100)^2(3 + R/100).
mistakes: Assuming CI is always double SI (not true; depends on rate and time).
Using the 2-year difference formula for 3 years.
Comparing SI and CI when compounding frequency differs without adjusting terms.

practice.question: A sum of Rs. 2,000 amounts to Rs. 2,400 in 4 years at simple interest. The rate of interest per annum is:
practice.explanation: SI = Amount - Principal = 2400 - 2000 = Rs. 400. Using SI = (P x R x T)/100: 400 = (2000 x R x 4)/100 = 80R. So R = 400/80 = 5% per annum.

practice.question: Find the compound interest on 1000 at 10% per annum for 2 years (annual compounding).
practice.explanation: Amount = P(1 + R/100)^T = 1000*(1.1)^2 = 1000*1.21 = 1210. CI = Amount - Principal = 1210 - 1000 = 210 (interest on interest adds 10 over simple interest of 200).
